# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |

# gh-396: Parity with dm.ai#710: env_get / env_list with one secret-aware policy (JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST)

## Description

Java added `env_get` / `env_list` (epam/dm.ai#710). JS agents had **no way to read configuration**: `ADO_PROJECT` from `dmtools.env` was unreachable, and ADO work items were created in the project `879` (the work item id) until the project came from `jira.project` instead (dmtools-agents#885). Please add the same tools to the Dart runtime with the **same policy**, because agents written for one runtime must behave identically on the other.

**Contract (identical to Java):**
- `env_get {name}` → `{"name":..,"value":..}` | `{"name":..,"error":..}`; `value` is `null` when unset; a refusal **never contains the value**. Name matching is case-insensitive; invalid names (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only) are rejected **without a lookup**.
- `env_list {}` → `{"names":[..]}` (+ `ignoredSecretLikeNames` when `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST` contains credential-looking names). Names only, never values.
- Integration tag `env`, always available (like `file` / `cli`).

**Single source of truth (the important part).**
1. **A name that looks like a secret is never readable**, whatever any allowlist says. Whole-word match on `_`-separated words: `TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASS, PAT, AUTH, LOGIN, CREDENTIAL(S), BEARER, COOKIE, SESSION, PRIVATE, CERT, SIGNATURE, PASSPHRASE` (+ any word ending in `TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/APIKEY`). Exceptions: `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT` (configuration, not credentials). `KEYBOARD` / `AUTHOR` are NOT secrets; null/blank fails closed. Copy the word list from Java `JsEnvPolicy` — do not re-derive it.
2. **Default allowlist = every configuration name the Dart `PropertyReader` declares, minus secrets** — derive it from the declared names, do not hand-maintain a second list (Dart has no reflection: generate the list from the same constants the reader uses, and add a test that fails when a constant is missing from it). In Java today that is 93 readable / 31 credential names.
3. **`JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST=A,B`** (env or `dmtools.env`) extends it; secret-looking entries are ignored.

**Tests to mirror (Java `JsEnvPolicyTest`, `EnvToolsTest`):** credential names are secret; `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` / `PROMPT_CHUNK_TOKEN_LIMIT` readable; whole-word matching; **no declared credential constant is ever allowed, even when put in `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST`** (sweep over all constants with the worst-case allowlist, asserting the value never appears in any answer); the default list contains every non-secret declared name; invalid names are rejected without a lookup; `env_list` never contains a value.

**Known limit (same on both runtimes, documented):** this stops accidental leaks, not a hostile script. A script that can run `bash` through `cli_execute_command` can read the environment another way, and `file_read` can read `dmtools.env` if it is in the working directory. Hardening those two is a separate, backward-compatibility-sensitive change (child tools such as `gh`/`git` legitimately need `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so it is NOT part of this parity item.

**Verified live on the Java jar from a JS agent:** `ADO_PROJECT` / `DEFAULT_TRACKER` readable, a custom name readable once allowlisted, `ADO_PAT_TOKEN` and an allowlisted `JIRA_API_TOKEN` refused, and the real PAT never appeared in the output.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |

# gh-396: Parity with dm.ai#710: env_get / env_list with one secret-aware policy (JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST)

## Description

Java added `env_get` / `env_list` (epam/dm.ai#710). JS agents had **no way to read configuration**: `ADO_PROJECT` from `dmtools.env` was unreachable, and ADO work items were created in the project `879` (the work item id) until the project came from `jira.project` instead (dmtools-agents#885). Please add the same tools to the Dart runtime with the **same policy**, because agents written for one runtime must behave identically on the other.

**Contract (identical to Java):**
- `env_get {name}` → `{"name":..,"value":..}` | `{"name":..,"error":..}`; `value` is `null` when unset; a refusal **never contains the value**. Name matching is case-insensitive; invalid names (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only) are rejected **without a lookup**.
- `env_list {}` → `{"names":[..]}` (+ `ignoredSecretLikeNames` when `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST` contains credential-looking names). Names only, never values.
- Integration tag `env`, always available (like `file` / `cli`).

**Single source of truth (the important part).**
1. **A name that looks like a secret is never readable**, whatever any allowlist says. Whole-word match on `_`-separated words: `TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASS, PAT, AUTH, LOGIN, CREDENTIAL(S), BEARER, COOKIE, SESSION, PRIVATE, CERT, SIGNATURE, PASSPHRASE` (+ any word ending in `TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/APIKEY`). Exceptions: `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT` (configuration, not credentials). `KEYBOARD` / `AUTHOR` are NOT secrets; null/blank fails closed. Copy the word list from Java `JsEnvPolicy` — do not re-derive it.
2. **Default allowlist = every configuration name the Dart `PropertyReader` declares, minus secrets** — derive it from the declared names, do not hand-maintain a second list (Dart has no reflection: generate the list from the same constants the reader uses, and add a test that fails when a constant is missing from it). In Java today that is 93 readable / 31 credential names.
3. **`JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST=A,B`** (env or `dmtools.env`) extends it; secret-looking entries are ignored.

**Tests to mirror (Java `JsEnvPolicyTest`, `EnvToolsTest`):** credential names are secret; `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` / `PROMPT_CHUNK_TOKEN_LIMIT` readable; whole-word matching; **no declared credential constant is ever allowed, even when put in `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST`** (sweep over all constants with the worst-case allowlist, asserting the value never appears in any answer); the default list contains every non-secret declared name; invalid names are rejected without a lookup; `env_list` never contains a value.

**Known limit (same on both runtimes, documented):** this stops accidental leaks, not a hostile script. A script that can run `bash` through `cli_execute_command` can read the environment another way, and `file_read` can read `dmtools.env` if it is in the working directory. Hardening those two is a separate, backward-compatibility-sensitive change (child tools such as `gh`/`git` legitimately need `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so it is NOT part of this parity item.

**Verified live on the Java jar from a JS agent:** `ADO_PROJECT` / `DEFAULT_TRACKER` readable, a custom name readable once allowlisted, `ADO_PAT_TOKEN` and an allowlisted `JIRA_API_TOKEN` refused, and the real PAT never appeared in the output.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |

# gh-396: Parity with dm.ai#710: env_get / env_list with one secret-aware policy (JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST)

## Description

Java added `env_get` / `env_list` (epam/dm.ai#710). JS agents had **no way to read configuration**: `ADO_PROJECT` from `dmtools.env` was unreachable, and ADO work items were created in the project `879` (the work item id) until the project came from `jira.project` instead (dmtools-agents#885). Please add the same tools to the Dart runtime with the **same policy**, because agents written for one runtime must behave identically on the other.

**Contract (identical to Java):**
- `env_get {name}` → `{"name":..,"value":..}` | `{"name":..,"error":..}`; `value` is `null` when unset; a refusal **never contains the value**. Name matching is case-insensitive; invalid names (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only) are rejected **without a lookup**.
- `env_list {}` → `{"names":[..]}` (+ `ignoredSecretLikeNames` when `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST` contains credential-looking names). Names only, never values.
- Integration tag `env`, always available (like `file` / `cli`).

**Single source of truth (the important part).**
1. **A name that looks like a secret is never readable**, whatever any allowlist says. Whole-word match on `_`-separated words: `TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASS, PAT, AUTH, LOGIN, CREDENTIAL(S), BEARER, COOKIE, SESSION, PRIVATE, CERT, SIGNATURE, PASSPHRASE` (+ any word ending in `TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/APIKEY`). Exceptions: `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT` (configuration, not credentials). `KEYBOARD` / `AUTHOR` are NOT secrets; null/blank fails closed. Copy the word list from Java `JsEnvPolicy` — do not re-derive it.
2. **Default allowlist = every configuration name the Dart `PropertyReader` declares, minus secrets** — derive it from the declared names, do not hand-maintain a second list (Dart has no reflection: generate the list from the same constants the reader uses, and add a test that fails when a constant is missing from it). In Java today that is 93 readable / 31 credential names.
3. **`JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST=A,B`** (env or `dmtools.env`) extends it; secret-looking entries are ignored.

**Tests to mirror (Java `JsEnvPolicyTest`, `EnvToolsTest`):** credential names are secret; `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` / `PROMPT_CHUNK_TOKEN_LIMIT` readable; whole-word matching; **no declared credential constant is ever allowed, even when put in `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST`** (sweep over all constants with the worst-case allowlist, asserting the value never appears in any answer); the default list contains every non-secret declared name; invalid names are rejected without a lookup; `env_list` never contains a value.

**Known limit (same on both runtimes, documented):** this stops accidental leaks, not a hostile script. A script that can run `bash` through `cli_execute_command` can read the environment another way, and `file_read` can read `dmtools.env` if it is in the working directory. Hardening those two is a separate, backward-compatibility-sensitive change (child tools such as `gh`/`git` legitimately need `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so it is NOT part of this parity item.

**Verified live on the Java jar from a JS agent:** `ADO_PROJECT` / `DEFAULT_TRACKER` readable, a custom name readable once allowlisted, `ADO_PAT_TOKEN` and an allowlisted `JIRA_API_TOKEN` refused, and the real PAT never appeared in the output.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |

# gh-396: Parity with dm.ai#710: env_get / env_list with one secret-aware policy (JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST)

## Description

Java added `env_get` / `env_list` (epam/dm.ai#710). JS agents had **no way to read configuration**: `ADO_PROJECT` from `dmtools.env` was unreachable, and ADO work items were created in the project `879` (the work item id) until the project came from `jira.project` instead (dmtools-agents#885). Please add the same tools to the Dart runtime with the **same policy**, because agents written for one runtime must behave identically on the other.

**Contract (identical to Java):**
- `env_get {name}` → `{"name":..,"value":..}` | `{"name":..,"error":..}`; `value` is `null` when unset; a refusal **never contains the value**. Name matching is case-insensitive; invalid names (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only) are rejected **without a lookup**.
- `env_list {}` → `{"names":[..]}` (+ `ignoredSecretLikeNames` when `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST` contains credential-looking names). Names only, never values.
- Integration tag `env`, always available (like `file` / `cli`).

**Single source of truth (the important part).**
1. **A name that looks like a secret is never readable**, whatever any allowlist says. Whole-word match on `_`-separated words: `TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASS, PAT, AUTH, LOGIN, CREDENTIAL(S), BEARER, COOKIE, SESSION, PRIVATE, CERT, SIGNATURE, PASSPHRASE` (+ any word ending in `TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/APIKEY`). Exceptions: `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT` (configuration, not credentials). `KEYBOARD` / `AUTHOR` are NOT secrets; null/blank fails closed. Copy the word list from Java `JsEnvPolicy` — do not re-derive it.
2. **Default allowlist = every configuration name the Dart `PropertyReader` declares, minus secrets** — derive it from the declared names, do not hand-maintain a second list (Dart has no reflection: generate the list from the same constants the reader uses, and add a test that fails when a constant is missing from it). In Java today that is 93 readable / 31 credential names.
3. **`JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST=A,B`** (env or `dmtools.env`) extends it; secret-looking entries are ignored.

**Tests to mirror (Java `JsEnvPolicyTest`, `EnvToolsTest`):** credential names are secret; `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` / `PROMPT_CHUNK_TOKEN_LIMIT` readable; whole-word matching; **no declared credential constant is ever allowed, even when put in `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST`** (sweep over all constants with the worst-case allowlist, asserting the value never appears in any answer); the default list contains every non-secret declared name; invalid names are rejected without a lookup; `env_list` never contains a value.

**Known limit (same on both runtimes, documented):** this stops accidental leaks, not a hostile script. A script that can run `bash` through `cli_execute_command` can read the environment another way, and `file_read` can read `dmtools.env` if it is in the working directory. Hardening those two is a separate, backward-compatibility-sensitive change (child tools such as `gh`/`git` legitimately need `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so it is NOT part of this parity item.

**Verified live on the Java jar from a JS agent:** `ADO_PROJECT` / `DEFAULT_TRACKER` readable, a custom name readable once allowlisted, `ADO_PAT_TOKEN` and an allowlisted `JIRA_API_TOKEN` refused, and the real PAT never appeared in the output.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |

{"command":"cd /home/runner/work/dmtools-dart/dmtools-dart/lib/src; names=$(grep -ohE "'[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,}'" config/property_reader*.dart | tr -d "'" | sort -u);
{
echo "/// Every configuration name the [PropertyReader] family reads — the single"
echo "/// source for both the reader's lookups and the JS \`env_get\` allowlist"
echo "/// (\`JsEnvPolicy.defaultAllowed\`), so a new property cannot be read by the"
echo "/// reader yet missing from the allowlist."
echo "///"
echo "/// Generated from the reader's former string literals; add new names here,"
echo "/// then use the constant in the reader. The \`property_names_test\` fails when a"
echo "/// reader literal is not declared here."
echo "library;"
echo ""
echo "/// Configuration property names (Java \`PropertyReader\` constant parity)."
echo "class PropertyNames {"
echo "  PropertyNames._();"
echo ""
for n in $names; do echo "  static const String $n = '$n';"; done
echo ""
echo "  /// Every declared name, in declaration order."
echo "  static const List<String> all = ["
for n in $names; do echo "    $n,"; done
echo "  ];"
echo "}"
} > config/property_names.dart
for f in config/property_reader.dart config/property_reader_getters.dart config/property_reader_ai_getters.dart; do
  for n in $names; do sed -i "s/'$n'/PropertyNames.$n/g" $f; done
done
grep -c "PropertyNames\." config/property_reader*.dart; grep -nE "'[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,}'" config/property_reader*.dart | head"}

# gh-396: Parity with dm.ai#710: env_get / env_list with one secret-aware policy (JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST)

## Description

Java added `env_get` / `env_list` (epam/dm.ai#710). JS agents had **no way to read configuration**: `ADO_PROJECT` from `dmtools.env` was unreachable, and ADO work items were created in the project `879` (the work item id) until the project came from `jira.project` instead (dmtools-agents#885). Please add the same tools to the Dart runtime with the **same policy**, because agents written for one runtime must behave identically on the other.

**Contract (identical to Java):**
- `env_get {name}` → `{"name":..,"value":..}` | `{"name":..,"error":..}`; `value` is `null` when unset; a refusal **never contains the value**. Name matching is case-insensitive; invalid names (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only) are rejected **without a lookup**.
- `env_list {}` → `{"names":[..]}` (+ `ignoredSecretLikeNames` when `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST` contains credential-looking names). Names only, never values.
- Integration tag `env`, always available (like `file` / `cli`).

**Single source of truth (the important part).**
1. **A name that looks like a secret is never readable**, whatever any allowlist says. Whole-word match on `_`-separated words: `TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASS, PAT, AUTH, LOGIN, CREDENTIAL(S), BEARER, COOKIE, SESSION, PRIVATE, CERT, SIGNATURE, PASSPHRASE` (+ any word ending in `TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/APIKEY`). Exceptions: `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT` (configuration, not credentials). `KEYBOARD` / `AUTHOR` are NOT secrets; null/blank fails closed. Copy the word list from Java `JsEnvPolicy` — do not re-derive it.
2. **Default allowlist = every configuration name the Dart `PropertyReader` declares, minus secrets** — derive it from the declared names, do not hand-maintain a second list (Dart has no reflection: generate the list from the same constants the reader uses, and add a test that fails when a constant is missing from it). In Java today that is 93 readable / 31 credential names.
3. **`JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST=A,B`** (env or `dmtools.env`) extends it; secret-looking entries are ignored.

**Tests to mirror (Java `JsEnvPolicyTest`, `EnvToolsTest`):** credential names are secret; `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` / `PROMPT_CHUNK_TOKEN_LIMIT` readable; whole-word matching; **no declared credential constant is ever allowed, even when put in `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST`** (sweep over all constants with the worst-case allowlist, asserting the value never appears in any answer); the default list contains every non-secret declared name; invalid names are rejected without a lookup; `env_list` never contains a value.

**Known limit (same on both runtimes, documented):** this stops accidental leaks, not a hostile script. A script that can run `bash` through `cli_execute_command` can read the environment another way, and `file_read` can read `dmtools.env` if it is in the working directory. Hardening those two is a separate, backward-compatibility-sensitive change (child tools such as `gh`/`git` legitimately need `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so it is NOT part of this parity item.

**Verified live on the Java jar from a JS agent:** `ADO_PROJECT` / `DEFAULT_TRACKER` readable, a custom name readable once allowlisted, `ADO_PAT_TOKEN` and an allowlisted `JIRA_API_TOKEN` refused, and the real PAT never appeared in the output.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the

# gh-396: Parity with dm.ai#710: env_get / env_list with one secret-aware policy (JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST)

## Description

Java added `env_get` / `env_list` (epam/dm.ai#710). JS agents had **no way to read configuration**: `ADO_PROJECT` from `dmtools.env` was unreachable, and ADO work items were created in the project `879` (the work item id) until the project came from `jira.project` instead (dmtools-agents#885). Please add the same tools to the Dart runtime with the **same policy**, because agents written for one runtime must behave identically on the other.

**Contract (identical to Java):**
- `env_get {name}` → `{"name":..,"value":..}` | `{"name":..,"error":..}`; `value` is `null` when unset; a refusal **never contains the value**. Name matching is case-insensitive; invalid names (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only) are rejected **without a lookup**.
- `env_list {}` → `{"names":[..]}` (+ `ignoredSecretLikeNames` when `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST` contains credential-looking names). Names only, never values.
- Integration tag `env`, always available (like `file` / `cli`).

**Single source of truth (the important part).**
1. **A name that looks like a secret is never readable**, whatever any allowlist says. Whole-word match on `_`-separated words: `TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASS, PAT, AUTH, LOGIN, CREDENTIAL(S), BEARER, COOKIE, SESSION, PRIVATE, CERT, SIGNATURE, PASSPHRASE` (+ any word ending in `TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/APIKEY`). Exceptions: `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT` (configuration, not credentials). `KEYBOARD` / `AUTHOR` are NOT secrets; null/blank fails closed. Copy the word list from Java `JsEnvPolicy` — do not re-derive it.
2. **Default allowlist = every configuration name the Dart `PropertyReader` declares, minus secrets** — derive it from the declared names, do not hand-maintain a second list (Dart has no reflection: generate the list from the same constants the reader uses, and add a test that fails when a constant is missing from it). In Java today that is 93 readable / 31 credential names.
3. **`JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST=A,B`** (env or `dmtools.env`) extends it; secret-looking entries are ignored.

**Tests to mirror (Java `JsEnvPolicyTest`, `EnvToolsTest`):** credential names are secret; `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` / `PROMPT_CHUNK_TOKEN_LIMIT` readable; whole-word matching; **no declared credential constant is ever allowed, even when put in `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST`** (sweep over all constants with the worst-case allowlist, asserting the value never appears in any answer); the default list contains every non-secret declared name; invalid names are rejected without a lookup; `env_list` never contains a value.

**Known limit (same on both runtimes, documented):** this stops accidental leaks, not a hostile script. A script that can run `bash` through `cli_execute_command` can read the environment another way, and `file_read` can read `dmtools.env` if it is in the working directory. Hardening those two is a separate, backward-compatibility-sensitive change (child tools such as `gh`/`git` legitimately need `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so it is NOT part of this parity item.

**Verified live on the Java jar from a JS agent:** `ADO_PROJECT` / `DEFAULT_TRACKER` readable, a custom name readable once allowlisted, `ADO_PAT_TOKEN` and an allowlisted `JIRA_API_TOKEN` refused, and the real PAT never appeared in the output.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |

# gh-396: Parity with dm.ai#710: env_get / env_list with one secret-aware policy (JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST)

## Description

Java added `env_get` / `env_list` (epam/dm.ai#710). JS agents had **no way to read configuration**: `ADO_PROJECT` from `dmtools.env` was unreachable, and ADO work items were created in the project `879` (the work item id) until the project came from `jira.project` instead (dmtools-agents#885). Please add the same tools to the Dart runtime with the **same policy**, because agents written for one runtime must behave identically on the other.

**Contract (identical to Java):**
- `env_get {name}` → `{"name":..,"value":..}` | `{"name":..,"error":..}`; `value` is `null` when unset; a refusal **never contains the value**. Name matching is case-insensitive; invalid names (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only) are rejected **without a lookup**.
- `env_list {}` → `{"names":[..]}` (+ `ignoredSecretLikeNames` when `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST` contains credential-looking names). Names only, never values.
- Integration tag `env`, always available (like `file` / `cli`).

**Single source of truth (the important part).**
1. **A name that looks like a secret is never readable**, whatever any allowlist says. Whole-word match on `_`-separated words: `TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASS, PAT, AUTH, LOGIN, CREDENTIAL(S), BEARER, COOKIE, SESSION, PRIVATE, CERT, SIGNATURE, PASSPHRASE` (+ any word ending in `TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/APIKEY`). Exceptions: `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT` (configuration, not credentials). `KEYBOARD` / `AUTHOR` are NOT secrets; null/blank fails closed. Copy the word list from Java `JsEnvPolicy` — do not re-derive it.
2. **Default allowlist = every configuration name the Dart `PropertyReader` declares, minus secrets** — derive it from the declared names, do not hand-maintain a second list (Dart has no reflection: generate the list from the same constants the reader uses, and add a test that fails when a constant is missing from it). In Java today that is 93 readable / 31 credential names.
3. **`JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST=A,B`** (env or `dmtools.env`) extends it; secret-looking entries are ignored.

**Tests to mirror (Java `JsEnvPolicyTest`, `EnvToolsTest`):** credential names are secret; `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` / `PROMPT_CHUNK_TOKEN_LIMIT` readable; whole-word matching; **no declared credential constant is ever allowed, even when put in `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST`** (sweep over all constants with the worst-case allowlist, asserting the value never appears in any answer); the default list contains every non-secret declared name; invalid names are rejected without a lookup; `env_list` never contains a value.

**Known limit (same on both runtimes, documented):** this stops accidental leaks, not a hostile script. A script that can run `bash` through `cli_execute_command` can read the environment another way, and `file_read` can read `dmtools.env` if it is in the working directory. Hardening those two is a separate, backward-compatibility-sensitive change (child tools such as `gh`/`git` legitimately need `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so it is NOT part of this parity item.

**Verified live on the Java jar from a JS agent:** `ADO_PROJECT` / `DEFAULT_TRACKER` readable, a custom name readable once allowlisted, `ADO_PAT_TOKEN` and an allowlisted `JIRA_API_TOKEN` refused, and the real PAT never appeared in the output.

# AGENTS.md — rules for working in dmtools-dart

Pure Dart port of DMTools (Java/GraalJS → Dart/QuickJS). **Read `GOAL.md` first —
it is the spec.** This file is the operating manual: rules, commands, layout.

---

## 1. Non-negotiable rules

1. **crap4dart is law.** CRAP threshold **8.0** (`crap4dart.yaml`), tool
   pinned to **0.9.5** in CI (and locally; keep both in sync). Pre-commit hook
   runs `crap4dart check --staged`; CI runs `check --all` + `analyze` on every push.
   Never commit on red, never weaken a gate to make code pass. Known
   exemptions live in `crap4dart.yaml` with comments (Java-parity client
   classes → class_size warning; testrail_create_case* Java-parity
   @MCPParam signatures → method_size max_params override).
2. **Signature parity with Java DMTools.** Config JSON keys, tool names
   (snake_case), env variables, CLI commands — identical to the Java version.
   A config or `dmtools.env` that works with Java must work unchanged here.
   When behavior is ambiguous, **the Java source is the spec**; record the decision
   in the commit message.
3. **No JVM, no GraalVM.** Dart only. JS runtime is QuickJS via `dart:ffi` with
   synchronous host calls (not the `flutter_js` plugin), consumed from the
   **`quickjs_runtime` package** (github.com/IstiN/quickjs_runtime, git dep in
   `pubspec.yaml`) — never vendored here. Build the native library with
   `make native` (or `bash "$QUICKJS_PKG/tool/build_quickjs.sh"`); the .so is
   built inside the package checkout and found via
   `.dart_tool/package_config.json` (override with `JSR_QUICKJS_LIB`).
4. **Thin `bin/`.** CI coverage is collected with `--report-on lib`, so `bin/` is
   outside LCOV. All logic lives in `lib/`; `bin/` only parses argv and delegates.
5. **Tests ship with code.** Coverage gate is 80% (`gates.test_coverage`).
   Test code is held to the same bar (`sources: [lib, bin, test]`).
6. **Never commit secrets.** `dmtools.env` / `dmtools-local.env` are git-ignored;
   keep them that way. Credentials in tests come only from the standard config
   resolution chain (see GOAL.md → Integration testing strategy).

## 2. Where things are

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GOAL.md` | **The spec**: mission, constraints, audit facts, phases 0–5, test strategy |
| `crap4dart.yaml` | Quality gate config (threshold 8.0, sources lib/bin/test) |
| `.github/workflows/quality.yml` | CI: format → analyze → test+coverage → crap4dart |
| `bin/dmtools.dart` | CLI entry (stub; full JobRunner surface = Phase 2) |
| `install.sh` | One-line installer: prebuilt AOT binaries from GitHub Releases (see `release-cli.yml` / `install-test.yml`) |
| `lib/` | All implementation code |
| `test/` | `dart test` suite (L1 unit; L2 contract fixtures later) |

Java reference implementation (read-only, the spec for behavior):
**https://github.com/epam/dm.ai** — clone it fresh (always the latest upstream);
key files are named per phase in GOAL.md (e.g. `PropertyReader.java`,
`JobRunner.java`, `JobJavaScriptBridge.java`, `cliagent/CliAgent.java`).
Agent scripts and the JS test suite: **https://github.com/IstiN/dmtools-agents**.
JS runtime (`jsr`) extensions go to **https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_js_widget_runtime**
via fork + PR — never vendored here (see GOAL.md).

## 3. Local dev loop

```bash
export PATH="$HOME/.pub-cache/bin:$PATH"   # crap4dart lives here; without it the
                                           # pre-commit hook SKIPS checks silently

dart pub get
make native                               # build the QuickJS .so (quickjs_runtime pkg)
dart format .                              # CI fails on unformatted code
dart analyze
dart test --coverage=coverage
dart pub global run coverage:format_coverage \
  --lcov --in coverage --out coverage/lcov.info --report-on lib
crap4dart check --all                      # gates (fast, no network)
crap4dart analyze                          # CRAP scores, threshold 8.0
```

If crap4dart is missing: `dart pub global activate crap4dart`.

## 4. Commit & CI discipline

- Small, focused commits; message states *what* and *why* (and the Java file that
  served as spec, when porting behavior).
- The hook runs only on staged files — CI runs everything, so run the full local
  loop above before pushing.
- CI red = stop and fix; no merging on red.
- `git commit --no-verify` is a code smell; if you use it, say why in the message.

## 5. Current status & next work

**All 5 phases implemented.** 387 canonical MCP tools across 17 integrations
(no dmtools-agents tool call remains uncovered; the Java↔Dart gap snapshot in
`test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_gaps.txt` tracks the remaining non-agent names).
QuickJS runtime via dart:ffi with sync callbacks — dmtools-agents suite passes
unmodified (751 tests green). CliAgent lifecycle fully
ported (incl. timer/error/line JS actions). `dmtools run`, `list`, `doctor`,
`--version`, `--help`, `--list-jobs` all functional.

**Sync dispatch** (`executeToolViaJava`): `SyncToolDispatcher` routes by
prefix to self-contained per-integration classes in `lib/src/js/sync_tools/`
(jira, github, gitlab, ado, confluence, bitrise, jenkins) plus per-provider
`<provider>_ai_chat` — HTTP via curl subprocess inside NativeCallable
callbacks, `file_*`/`cli_*` via `SyncToolDispatcher.nonHttpHandler`. The
JS bridge (`JobJavaScriptBridge` parity): CommonJS `require` loader
(`require_loader.dart`), JSRunner context (`ticket`/`response`/`initiator`/
`inputJql`/`metadata`), inline/URL/file jsPath, action() contract, JS-visible
host-fn validation errors (`__jsError` sentinel), alias tool wrappers.

**Remaining work** (diminishing returns, in priority order):
1. InstructionProcessor
2. Integration test layer (L2 contract tests, L3 live integration)
3. Re-extract `test/fixtures/java_mcp_tool_names.txt` when Java gains new
   @MCPTools and port what the gap snapshot then reports

Phase checkboxes live in GOAL.md — tick them as you complete items and keep the
file current when a decision changes the plan.

## 6. Testing layers (so you put each test in the right place)

| Layer | Location | Runs where |
|---|---|---|
| L1 unit | `test/`, mocked | pre-commit + CI quality.yml |
| L2 contract | `test/` with recorded Java fixtures | CI quality.yml |
| L3 live integration | `test/` `@Tags(['integration'])`, creds via env/`dmtools.env` | nightly + manual, excluded by default via `dart_test.yaml` |

# gh-396: Parity with dm.ai#710: env_get / env_list with one secret-aware policy (JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST)

## Description

Java added `env_get` / `env_list` (epam/dm.ai#710). JS agents had **no way to read configuration**: `ADO_PROJECT` from `dmtools.env` was unreachable, and ADO work items were created in the project `879` (the work item id) until the project came from `jira.project` instead (dmtools-agents#885). Please add the same tools to the Dart runtime with the **same policy**, because agents written for one runtime must behave identically on the other.

**Contract (identical to Java):**
- `env_get {name}` → `{"name":..,"value":..}` | `{"name":..,"error":..}`; `value` is `null` when unset; a refusal **never contains the value**. Name matching is case-insensitive; invalid names (`[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9_]*` only) are rejected **without a lookup**.
- `env_list {}` → `{"names":[..]}` (+ `ignoredSecretLikeNames` when `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST` contains credential-looking names). Names only, never values.
- Integration tag `env`, always available (like `file` / `cli`).

**Single source of truth (the important part).**
1. **A name that looks like a secret is never readable**, whatever any allowlist says. Whole-word match on `_`-separated words: `TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASS, PAT, AUTH, LOGIN, CREDENTIAL(S), BEARER, COOKIE, SESSION, PRIVATE, CERT, SIGNATURE, PASSPHRASE` (+ any word ending in `TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/APIKEY`). Exceptions: `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT` (configuration, not credentials). `KEYBOARD` / `AUTHOR` are NOT secrets; null/blank fails closed. Copy the word list from Java `JsEnvPolicy` — do not re-derive it.
2. **Default allowlist = every configuration name the Dart `PropertyReader` declares, minus secrets** — derive it from the declared names, do not hand-maintain a second list (Dart has no reflection: generate the list from the same constants the reader uses, and add a test that fails when a constant is missing from it). In Java today that is 93 readable / 31 credential names.
3. **`JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST=A,B`** (env or `dmtools.env`) extends it; secret-looking entries are ignored.

**Tests to mirror (Java `JsEnvPolicyTest`, `EnvToolsTest`):** credential names are secret; `OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS` / `PROMPT_CHUNK_TOKEN_LIMIT` readable; whole-word matching; **no declared credential constant is ever allowed, even when put in `JS_ENV_ALLOWLIST`** (sweep over all constants with the worst-case allowlist, asserting the value never appears in any answer); the default list contains every non-secret declared name; invalid names are rejected without a lookup; `env_list` never contains a value.

**Known limit (same on both runtimes, documented):** this stops accidental leaks, not a hostile script. A script that can run `bash` through `cli_execute_command` can read the environment another way, and `file_read` can read `dmtools.env` if it is in the working directory. Hardening those two is a separate, backward-compatibility-sensitive change (child tools such as `gh`/`git` legitimately need `GITHUB_TOKEN`), so it is NOT part of this parity item.

**Verified live on the Java jar from a JS agent:** `ADO_PROJECT` / `DEFAULT_TRACKER` readable, a custom name readable once allowlisted, `ADO_PAT_TOKEN` and an allowlisted `JIRA_API_TOKEN` refused, and the real PAT never appeared in the output.

Names only, never values.\n- Integration tag `env`, always available (like `file` / `cli`).\n\n**Single source of truth (the important part).**\n1. **A name that looks like a secret is never readable**, whatever any allowlist says. Whole-word match on `_`-separated words: `TOKEN, KEY, SECRET, PASSWORD, PASS, PAT, AUTH, LOGIN, CREDENTIAL(S), BEARER, COOKIE, SESSION, PRIVATE, CERT, SIGNATURE, PASSPHRASE` (+ any word ending in `TOKEN/SECRET/PASSWORD/APIKEY`). Exceptions: `*_MAX_TOKENS` and `*_TOKEN_LIMIT` (configuration, not credentials). `KEYBOARD` / `AUTHOR` are NOT secrets; null/blank fails closed. Copy the word list from Java `JsEnvPolicy` — do not re-derive it.\n2. **Default allowlist = every configuration name the Dart `PropertyReader` declares, minus secrets** — derive it from the declared names, do not hand-maintain a second list (Dart has no reflection: generate the list from the same constants the reader uses, and add a test that fails when a constant is missing from it).
